top_story: Israeli strikes in southern Lebanon and the Bekaa Valley intensified on 23 May after months of attacks that had already devastated emergency services, with paramedics, ambulances, and hospitals repeatedly hit and civilians again killed near Tyre. This pattern is not only expanding physical destruction but also stripping communities of the capacity to rescue the wounded, making each new round of bombardment more lethal for civilians. Hours later, Trump’s claim that a US-Iran agreement is largely negotiated, including movement on the Strait of Hormuz, pointed to a possible regional de-escalation track but remained politically fragile as Iranian-linked messaging stressed Tehran’s continued control of the waterway. The contrast is stark: diplomacy may be edging forward at the Gulf level, but it has not restrained Israeli military pressure in Lebanon, leaving local populations exposed even as wider strategic bargaining advances.
